objections.claim: `added_corpus := normalise(join of every added line of every watched file, with single spaces)` concatenates all added lines of all files into one stream. A deleted block's text can then match across the seam between two unrelated added lines (even in different files), counting as "moved" when nothing was moved. This is a fail-open hole in a check whose stated principle is "Fail closed inside scope … It never turns into a pass." The fix costs nothing: build the corpus per watched file (or per added block) and test membership against each.

objections.predicted_consequence: a rare but real false pass on exactly the class of deletion the check exists to catch, contradicting the spec's own fail-closed commitment; reviewers cannot distinguish a genuine move from a seam artifact.

objections.claim: The check grants "pass" on the strength of the `## Rule inventory` rows in the committed spec, but the committed spec is written by the same agent whose PR it gates. An agent (or any PR author) that deletes a rule can satisfy the check by writing its own row — `dropped: <anything>`, or a `kept` row naming a real test that does not test the rule — quoting ≥20 characters of the deleted text. The check verifies only that the quote is a substring of the deleted prose and that named files exist; it cannot distinguish a truthful row from a fabricated one. Worse, rows are pooled across all committed specs with no file binding: a row in an unrelated old spec under the spec docs path covers deletions in any watched file, and one anchor matching duplicated text covers many blocks at once. The design principle "Coverage is mechanical; correctness stays with review" is the stated control, but it does not answer the threat: the reviewer sees a plausible-looking table and the mechanical gate adds zero adversarial resistance — it enforces the format, not the coverage, against a non-cooperative actor. The spec must establish who can write the input that grants the pass; it establishes only that the actor is the PR author.

objections.claim: The check applies only when the PR commits a spec under the spec docs path, and a PR that does not returns `skipped` with exit 0 (§3 exit table: "exit 0 pass or skipped"). In branch protection, exit 0 is a green required check — a skip is indistinguishable from a pass. So an agent PR that deletes skill prose and commits no spec sails through the gate. The spec's answer is that graft's `faff spec commit` always commits the spec, and a violation "is a graft defect to file, not a reason to change this scope" — but nothing in this check or in CI enforces that invariant; the gate's coverage rests entirely on an unverified precondition controlled by the gated actor. The precedent cited (`governance.yml` `on-missing: pass`) is a governance floor with a documented residual and a named flip-to-fail path; this spec states no such end-state and no detection beyond a human reading CI logs for `skipped_reason: "no-spec-committed"` on a PR that carries an anchor footprint.

occurrences.claim: The anchor floor and the coverage rule are inconsistent.
